title: Bounded proper base change from its sheaf case
statement: Under the same structural hypotheses on a Grothendieck abelian coefficient category A, let (g',f',f,g) be a Cartesian square of schemes with f proper. For a bounded object K of D(Sh(X_et,A)), suppose that for every integer q and every geometric point s of X a positive integer annihilates id(H^q(K)_s). Then the canonical unbounded derived base-change map Lg* Rf* K -> Rf'* Lg'* K is an isomorphism. The category, functors and exchange are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; properness is [def-weil-proper-morphism] and A is [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian].

source.place: XVII 4.3.2(ii), the reduction from bounded complexes to their homology sheaves by truncation; the coefficient-independent triangulated induction is implemented in Lean.

proof.text: Finite exponent of all geometric stalks is invariant under a sheaf isomorphism: conjugate the annihilating multiple of the identity by the stalk isomorphism. Apply the sheaf-level proper-base-change theorem to each homology sheaf of K placed in degree zero. The canonical exchange commutes with shifts, so it is invertible on that sheaf placed in any degree.

Apply the proved library Postnikov theorem DerivedCategory.exists_iteratedExtensions_of_bounded to K and the isomorphism-closed sheaf property P of finite-exponent geometric stalks. It expresses K as finitely many extensions of single objects M placed in various degrees, with P M. The theorem constructs this decomposition by canonical truncation triangles; it handles empty support as well, without requiring a termwise-torsion representative.

The exchange isomorphism locus NatTrans.isoLocus is a strictly full triangulated property because both composite functors are triangulated and the exchange commutes with shifts. Each single object in the Postnikov decomposition belongs to it by the sheaf theorem and the shift isomorphism of singleFunctors. Apply the proved library closure theorem DerivedCategory.iteratedExtensions_le to put K in this locus. This is the finite truncation/five-lemma argument, with its generic induction reused from the source library.

proof_origin.place: XVII 4.3.2(ii), finite truncation of a bounded complex into its homology sheaves; Lean reuses the proved library exists_iteratedExtensions_of_bounded, iteratedExtensions_le, and the triangulated isomorphism locus instead of reproving their inductions.

theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_of_bounded_stalkwise_finite_exponent
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} [IsProper f]
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : _root_.DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A))
    (hK : _root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded K)
    (hT : ∀ (n : ℤ) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
      (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X), ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧
        N • (𝟙 ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.obj
          ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj K))) = 0) :
    IsIso ((derivedBaseChangeMap A sq.toCommSq).app K)
